title: The Drowned Town
logline: In a dry year the water behind a dam drops, and the streets of a town that was flooded decades ago come back into the air. People who grew up there walk out across the cracked mud, looking for a house that is no longer where they remember it.

object.note: Object 4 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Every answer on the road came from where the person stood; next, people whose own map no longer matches the ground walk out across a drained reservoir looking for where home was.

thread_out.thread: From a reservoir's slow, silent mud to a wholesale market where lorries arrive all at once and attention scatters as fast as prices change.

requirements: A reservoir whose drawdown genuinely exposes the remains of a submerged settlement during the filming window
Former residents or their families willing to return and speak
Safe access onto the exposed bed and permission from the relevant authorities

suggestions.name: Victoria Reservoir (old Teldeniya area)
suggestions.why: A large Mahaweli reservoir whose construction submerged settlements; remains of the old town have been reported to reappear in severe droughts.
suggestions.season_notes: Only in drought years, when water levels fall far enough; unpredictable
suggestions.verify: Confirm which settlements were submerged, whether remains have actually re-emerged, and who manages access.

suggestions.name: Kotmale Reservoir area
suggestions.why: Another Mahaweli reservoir built over inhabited valleys; low water has reportedly exposed older structures.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Something you cannot see is not necessarily gone. The texts describe some states of mind as lying hidden, like a town under water, and rising again when conditions change.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: පෙනෙන්නට නැති දෙයක් නැති වී ගියා නොවේ; වතුරට යට වූ නගරයක් මෙන්, සිතේ සමහර ගති සැඟවී සිට සුදුසු අවස්ථාවක් ආ විට නැවත මතු වෙයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma speaks of latent tendencies (anusaya): unwholesome states that lie hidden in a person's mind-stream and rise again whenever a suitable object appears. Both texts describe three stages of a defilement: lying asleep, surfacing in the mind, and spilling over into word or act. Margaya gives the example of forest hermits, far from temptation and settled in meditation, who still fall from their calm when certain objects meet them, because what was held down had never been removed.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The waterline stain high on the hills tells the viewer how much was covered, and the dry year lets steps, a well and a doorway come back into the air. Former residents pace out streets and gently disagree about which foundation was whose, and the ground that seemed gone turns out to have been there all along. The first rain, when the water begins to return, leaves the viewer knowing the town is still there underneath.

key_terms.en: latent tendency; lies hidden until a suitable object appears
stage of surfacing in the mind / stage of spilling into act or speech

lesson.caution: The drowned town is an image, not a picture of anyone's mind: the residents' memories and grief are not defilements, and the texts do not say that the mind is pure underneath.
lesson.builds_on: The last film showed a mind that cannot settle on the road ahead; this one adds that what confuses us is often out of sight, lying low until conditions bring it back up.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
